card.lives_in: Chapel Allerton, Leeds, Yorkshire and The Humber
card.occupation: Speciality doctor in acute medicine at a large Leeds teaching hospital. She works long rotas, often 50 to 55 hours a week with on-calls, and picks up extra locum shifts when money is tight or she fancies a holiday.
card.education_detail: MBBS from the University of Nigeria, Enugu. Came to the UK at 26 to sit PLAB and did foundation-style trust jobs in Bradford before moving to Leeds. Has MRCP Part 1 and keeps meaning to finish Part 2.
card.household: Lives in a rented three-bed terrace with her partner of seven years, Tunde, a civil engineer for a rail contractor. Her cousin Adaeze, 24, has stayed in the box room for the past year while she does a nursing degree at Leeds Beckett. Chiamaka and Tunde are not married. A big wedding has been 'next year' for three years running.
card.cultural_background: Igbo, born and raised in Enugu, Nigeria. Eldest daughter of a secondary school headmistress and a pharmacist, both still in Enugu. Has lived in Yorkshire for 13 years and has British citizenship. Goes to a Pentecostal church in Leeds most Sundays she isn't on shift, mainly for the choir and the people. Sends money home and is the family's go-to person for medical questions on the WhatsApp group.
card.professional_persona: Warm, quick and popular on the ward. Nurses like her because she's friendly and remembers their kids' names. Very good with frightened patients and families, and she does get upset about the sad cases, sometimes crying in the car afterwards. Less good on paperwork: discharge summaries pile up and her portfolio for appraisal is always done the night before. She likes to be seen as the one who holds the ward together and will sometimes present a team effort as more her own than it was. Ambitious about status and pay and a bit resentful of colleagues who got consultant posts faster.
card.sports_persona: Not sporty. She has a gym membership she uses in bursts, mostly the group classes because they're sociable. Walks round Roundhay Park with Adaeze on days off. Will happily go to a Leeds Rhinos game if Tunde's mates have spare tickets, mainly for the atmosphere and the drinks after.
card.arts_persona: Sings alto in the church choir and loves it. Listens to Afrobeats, old highlife her dad played, and gospel in the car. Watches Nollywood films on Netflix and reality TV, especially Real Housewives and Love Island, which she'll defend loudly. Not a gallery person, though she went to The Hepworth once and enjoyed the café.
card.travel_persona: Goes back to Enugu roughly every 18 months, usually around Christmas, with suitcases full of gifts. Likes city breaks with friends where she can dress up and post photos, like Dubai, Lisbon and Barcelona. Books things late and has twice nearly missed a flight from Manchester Airport.
card.culinary_persona: Cooks big pots of jollof, egusi or oha soup on her day off and freezes portions, then forgets them and eats Deliveroo after late shifts. Calls the evening meal 'tea' half the time now without noticing. Loves a Sunday carvery with Tunde's colleagues. Has strong opinions on which Leeds African grocer has the best stockfish.
hobbies_and_interests: hosting friends for food and music
shopping for handbags and shoes she probably shouldn't buy
Instagram, mainly outfit and food posts
skills: cooking for twenty at short notice
talking her way into upgrades and discounts
card.career_goals: Wants to get onto a CESR or training route to become a consultant in acute medicine within five years, mostly for the title, pay and recognition. Also likes the idea of private aesthetics or medico-legal work on the side. Needs to finish MRCP Part 2 first and keeps putting it off.
card.voice: Fast, warm and animated, with a lot of laughter. Nigerian English accent softened by 13 years in Yorkshire, and some Leeds habits have crept in: 'knackered', 'tea' for the evening meal, the odd 'love' to patients. Uses 'erm' when thinking and 'you know' or 'do you know what I mean' as tags, sometimes 'sort of' to soften. Says 'sorry, sorry' to correct herself mid-sentence. Hates silence on a call and fills it with a joke or a follow-up question. Often echoes the interviewer's words back ('long hours? oh, long hours is my life'). Goes quieter and slower when something touches her emotionally.
card.typing: Quick and loose, usually from her phone. Mostly lowercase with the odd capital at the start. Skips apostrophes ('dont', 'im') and full stops at the end. Uses 'lol', 'tbh' and the occasional '!!' when she feels strongly. Typos left uncorrected, like 'teh' and 'definately'. Short answers unless the topic is work or family.
card.with_strangers: Instantly friendly and chatty, asks where you're from and finds a connection. Compliments easily and comes across as fun and open. Sprinkles in mentions of her job, recent trips or nice things in a way that can sound a little like showing off. Agreeable and rarely argues. If she disagrees she laughs it off rather than pushing back.
small_things: she's just come off a run of night shifts and is knackered
the parking at the hospital is a nightmare
she's been watching the new Love Island series

choir has a big Easter service coming up
the heating in the house is rubbish and the landlord won't sort it
she's craving suya and there's nowhere decent nearby
deeper_things: she worries she's left it late to have children and gets anxious when her mum brings it up
she cries after losing patients more than she lets colleagues see
she feels guilty about how little she visits her ageing parents
she's quietly frustrated that, as an overseas-trained doctor, she's had to work harder for less recognition
she's not sure if the wedding keeps getting postponed because of money or because Tunde isn't keen
she's spent more on credit cards than she'd admit to him
card.webcam_photo: Laptop webcam at a slightly low angle, so the frame catches her chin and the ceiling corner. She's sitting at a kitchen table in the evening, lit mainly by a warm overhead pendant light with a cooler glow from the screen on her face. Dark brown skin, round face, broad smile with teeth showing, eyebrows raised as if mid-laugh. Shoulder-length black box braids pulled into a loose high bun, with a few braids falling to one side. No glasses. Small gold hoop earrings. Navy NHS-style scrub top with a grey hoodie unzipped over it, and a lanyard still round her neck, tucked half inside the hoodie. Behind her is a fitted kitchen with cream cupboards, a kettle, a stack of unopened post by the bread bin, a fruit bowl with plantains and two satsumas, a fridge covered in magnets and a church choir rota, and a large Nigerian-flag tea towel hanging off the oven door. A doorway on the right shows part of a hallway with coats piled on a hook.
